+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8980'
+title: The frame decoder must not stop or crash on a bad header
+---
+## Problem
+- `FrameDecoder.extractNextMessage` (`Sources/FoundationModelsCodeContext/LSP/Wire.swift:116-138`) returns `nil` and removes no bytes when the header is not UTF-8 or when it has no number for `Content-Length` (`:121-126`). The decoder then waits for more bytes forever. All later messages from the server are lost, and the buffer grows with no limit.
+- Crash: `parseContentLength` (`:144-153`) accepts a negative number. With `Content-Length: -5`, `bodyEnd` is less than `bodyStart`, and the range at `:135` stops the process with a trap.
+- The test mock server has its own header parser (`Tests/.../scripted-lsp-server.swift:99-103`).
+
+## Change
+- On a bad header block, remove the header block (up to and with the blank line) from the buffer, record the error, and continue with the next frame. Log the error one time for each bad frame, with no payload text.
+- Reject a negative `Content-Length` and a value that is larger than a maximum (for example 64 MiB). Treat it as a bad header.
+- Keep one header parser. If possible, let the test mock use the same framing code.
+
+## Tests
+- Send a frame with `Content-Length: abc`, then a good frame. The decoder gives the good frame.
+- Send a frame with `Content-Length: -5`, then a good frame. There is no crash, and the decoder gives the good frame.
+- Send a header that is not UTF-8, then a good frame. The decoder gives the good frame.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+- [ ] A bad header does not stop the decoder.
+- [ ] A negative or too large length does not crash the process.
+- [ ] The tests above pass.
+
+#lsp-fix
\ No newline at end of file

+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m56qj7rr7266jhycps25azrk
+  text: |-
+    Research done.
+    - The daemon finds a dead server only through `isAlive` (`process.isRunning`) in `healthCheck()`. `healthCheck()` sets `handle = nil` and does not call `terminate`. Thus after a bad header the connection must kill the process itself, else the daemon never restarts it.
+    - The reader loop runs on a dedicated thread outside the actor. Plan: the decoder throws `JSONRPCFrameError` and clears its buffer; the reader loop logs one `.error` record (server, direction, error case, no payload), fails all pending requests, and asks the actor to `close()` (SIGKILL, close pipes, finish notifications).
+    - With `Content-Length: -5` the old code traps in `buffer[bodyStart..<bodyEnd]`, so the RED connection test crashes the test process.
+    - The mock runs as `swift <one file>`. `swift a.swift b.swift` does not compile two files (tested: "cannot find 'helper' in scope"). To share the framing code, move the decoder and `frame(payload:)` to a new file `LSP/Framing.swift` that imports only Foundation, and let the unit test target and the integration package join that file with the mock into one script file below `/tmp` before they start it.
+    - Also add a limit on the header length (no `\r\n\r\n` in the stream), because without it the buffer also grows with no limit.
